title: Select the simplest useful dryer model
equipment: Continuous conveyor drying tunnel with heated-air demand and product-zone temperature measurement
physicalPurpose: Represent the dryer delay, dominant thermal lag, and steady gain with the least model complexity that predicts independent data.
objective: Fit and independently validate first-order, first-order-plus-dead-time (FOPDT), second-order, and integrating candidates for a conveyor dryer, then select or reject by predeclared evidence gates.

simplifications: One local transport delay and one dominant thermal lag
Fixed belt speed, air flow, moisture load, sensor location, and measurement-noise amplitude
No spatial profile, humidity state, combustion dynamics, product-dependent gain, or actuator dynamics

baseline.limitation: Training error alone can reward missing physics or unnecessary parameter freedom.

change.decision: Select the least complex physically plausible candidate that passes residual and independent-prediction gates.

abortPredicates: Any required sample is nonfinite or has invalid quality
Heater or temperature leaves the declared operating region
Belt speed, air flow, moisture load, or another confounding input changes
Sample interval or included sample set differs between candidates
safety.restorationMode: Restore 30 percent heater demand and wait for the qualified 80 degC baseline
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer and dryer operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The project cannot authorise physical heater excitation
Physical testing requires reviewed combustion, temperature, airflow, belt, fire, product, personnel, and emergency procedures plus immediate approval

video.viewerOutcome: Reject underfit, integrating, and unjustified higher-order candidates using independent dryer evidence.

learning.context: A conveyor dryer has a repeatable transport delay, dominant thermal lag, steady gain, and bounded noisy temperature measurement.
learning.reason: Qualified excitation still permits several candidate structures, and fitting error alone can reward underfit or overfit.
theory: Structure is chosen before parameters; estimation data choose parameters while independent validation data test prediction.
RMSE, residual bias, residual autocorrelation, parameter uncertainty, equilibrium behavior, and physical plausibility answer different questions.
Extra complexity requires at least 10 percent independent improvement and removal of a repeatable residual feature.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict a 4 degC rise after 4 s delay, first-order early bias, integrating equilibrium failure, and FOPDT as the likely simplest adequate candidate.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, signals, units, 100 ms sampling, operating region, quality, noise, load, initial state, and seed.
Freeze common estimation samples, weights, candidate set, validation pulse, and decision thresholds before fitting.
learning.baseline: Rank candidates by estimation error alone and expose why that result is not a defensible model selection.
learning.change: Compare the same candidates using independent pulse prediction, residual structure, parameter uncertainty, equilibrium behavior, and the predeclared complexity rule.
learning.comparison: Retain all estimates, uncertainty, estimation and validation RMSE, bias, lag-one autocorrelation, delay-window bias, stability, plausibility, and reasons.
learning.validation: Require recovered FOPDT 0.40/12.0/4.0, validation RMSE 0.0508 degC and bias -0.0004 degC; reject first-order delay bias -0.2233, second-order RMSE 0.0729 without improvement, and integrating restoration error 1.200 degC.
learning.explanation: The selected FOPDT preserves repeatable delay, lag, and gain and predicts independent data without unjustified extra modes.
learning.transfer: Lesson 40 rejects candidate fitting when excitation or closed-loop correlation makes parameters unidentifiable.
